styles: Write in Colleen Hoover's raw emotional style with short punchy sentences and deep POV. Focus on internal conflict, messy relationships, and gut-wrenching emotional revelations. Use present tense for immediacy. Break readers' hearts then piece them back together.

Write in Nicholas Sparks' nostalgic heartwarming style with vivid descriptions of small-town settings and sweeping romantic gestures. Layer in bittersweet backstories, family dynamics, and fate-driven love. Make readers believe in soulmates.

Write in Emily Henry's witty contemporary style with snappy dialogue, slow-burn tension, and career-driven heroines. Balance humor with emotional depth. Create enemies-to-lovers or second-chance dynamics with sharp banter.

Write in Brandon Sanderson's detailed magic system style with logical world-building, intricate plot structures, and satisfying payoffs. Explain power mechanics clearly. Build epic ensemble casts with distinct character arcs.

Write in Sarah J. Maas' action-packed romantic fantasy style with fierce heroines, swoon-worthy love interests, and High stakes battles. Layer in courtly intrigue, chosen-one prophecies, and steamy romance. Use vivid combat scenes.

Write in a fast-paced contemporary urban style with gritty city settings, ambitious protagonists, and workplace/social dynamics. Focus on modern relationships, career challenges, and personal growth in metropolitan environments.

Write in Christina Lauren's playful rom-com style with quirky meet-cutes, workplace romance, and friends-to-lovers dynamics. Use dual POV, sexual tension, and laugh-out-loud moments balanced with genuine emotion.

Write in Andy Weir's science-grounded style with technical problem-solving, snarky humor, and survival scenarios. Make complex science accessible and exciting. Focus on human ingenuity against impossible odds.

Write in Pierce Brown's dark dystopian style with class warfare, political intrigue, and morally complex characters. Create brutal worlds with revolution themes. Use visceral action and strategic plotting.

Write in Gillian Flynn's psychological thriller style with unreliable narrators, dark twists, and morally ambiguous characters. Build paranoia and suspicion. Reveal shocking truths that recontextualize everything.
Write in Ruth Ware's atmospheric locked-room mystery style with claustrophobic settings, mounting dread, and cleverly planted clues. Use snowballing tension and shocking revelations.

Write in Stephen King's character-driven horror style with ordinary people facing extraordinary evil. Build dread slowly, focus on psychological terror, and create memorable monsters (human or otherwise). Ground scares in emotional truth.
Write in Paul Tremblay's ambiguous cosmic horror style with unreliable perspectives, open-ended mysteries, and existential dread. Leave readers unsettled and questioning reality.

Write in a thrilling adventure style with globe-trotting treasure hunts, historical mysteries, and non-stop action. Combine archaeology, cutting-edge science, and conspiracy theories. Create larger-than-life heroes.

Write in James Rollins' techno-thriller adventure style with scientific discoveries, ancient secrets, and race-against-time plotting. Blend history, mythology, and modern technology into explosive scenarios.

Write in Philippa Gregory's intimate historical style focusing on women's perspectives in royal courts. Rich period detail, political intrigue, and personal ambition. Make history feel immediate and personal.

Write in Ken Follett's epic historical style with sweeping multi-generational sagas, architectural/engineering details, and common people shaping history. Interweave multiple storylines across decades.
Write in a hard-boiled detective style with procedural accuracy, street-smart protagonists, and gritty urban crime. Focus on case-solving, moral complexity, and the toll of violence on investigators.
Write in Tana French's literary crime style with rich characterization, Dublin settings, and psychological depth. Make the investigation inseparable from character development. Use lyrical prose.

Write in Casey McQuiston's joyful queer rom-com style with charming leads, witty banter, and heartfelt coming-out journeys. Balance humor with genuine emotional stakes. Create swoony romance and found family.
Write in Adam Silvera's emotional YA style with diverse queer characters, magical realism elements, and themes of identity, loss, and first love. Make readers laugh and cry in equal measure.

Write in an urban fantasy paranormal style with supernatural creatures integrated into modern society. Sassy protagonists, romantic subplots, and mystery-solving in magical communities. Balance world-building with character-driven plots.

Write in Kim Harrison's complex paranormal style with witch/vampire/demon politics, morally grey protagonists, and intricate magic systems. Create dangerous romantic tension and high-stakes supernatural conflicts.

Write in a LitRPG system style with clear stat progression, skill trees, and game mechanics. Show character growth through quantifiable power-ups. Include status screens, quest notifications, and strategic combat using abilities.

Write in a progression fantasy style focusing on cultivation/leveling systems, power rankings, and martial arts. Emphasize training arcs, breakthrough moments, and satisfying power escalation against increasingly strong foes.

Write in a regression/reborn style where the protagonist returns to the past with future knowledge. Focus on correcting past mistakes, gaining advantages through foresight, and changing fate. Show strategic planning and satisfying payback.

Write in a reincarnation style with the protagonist reborn into a new life/world. Emphasize adapting to new circumstances, using past-life knowledge cleverly, and building a better future. Include moments of recognition and revelation.

Write in a calculated revenge style with meticulous planning, strategic manipulation, and satisfying takedowns of enemies. Show the protagonist's transformation from victim to powerful player. Balance ruthlessness with moments of humanity.

Write in a fast-paced revenge thriller style with visceral confrontations, escalating stakes, and cathartic justice. Create sympathetic motivations for vengeance while exploring moral costs. Build tension toward explosive payoffs.

Write in a passionate fanfiction style with intense character focus, slow-burn or fast-burn romance, and deep exploration of 'what-if' scenarios. Use close POV, emotional intensity, and fan-favorite tropes (enemies-to-lovers, forced proximity, etc.).

Write in an AU (Alternate Universe) fanfiction style that reimagines characters in completely new settings. Maintain core character traits while exploring fresh dynamics. Focus on relationship development and creative world-building.
